chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
You have been made to see if you care to see; you have been guided if you care to take guidance; and you have been made to hear if you care to lend your ears.

key_terms.أُسْمِعْتُمْ: You have been made to hear
key_terms.بُصَّرْتُمْ: You have been made to see (inner insight)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between divine provision of senses and human responsibility in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) emphasizes that the prerequisites for guidance—sight, hearing, and intellect—are already endowed by God, making spiritual success contingent upon human agency and active heedfulness. This reflects the Shia theological principle of 'Tawassul' through natural faculties, where divine grace provides the capacity, but human choice determines the outcome. The statement underscores that guidance is not merely a passive bestowal but a dynamic process requiring the individual to utilize their God-given senses to perceive truth.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 157. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him,

said: Surely, you have been made to see if (only) you care to see; surely, you have been guided if (only) you care to take guidance; and surely, you have been made to hear if (only) you care to lend your ears.
